## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Use the original tournament and enumerate all directed triangles in O(n^3) time. The empty tournament has optimum zero and the empty witness.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n)$ |
| Clauses | $O(n^3+n)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. A shortest directed cycle in a tournament is a directed triangle: the arc between its first and third vertices otherwise supplies a shorter cycle or a triangle. Since deleting vertices retains a tournament, deleting all directed triangles is equivalent to removing every directed cycle.

2. Use one deletion variable per vertex and the clause $x_a\vee x_b\vee x_c$ for each directed triangle. For threshold b add $\sum_v x_v\le b$ with the linear-size cardinality circuit. No auxiliary variable is introduced for a triangle.

3. Each threshold query has N=O(n), M=O(n^3+n), and width at most three, including all gate variables. Its bit length is O((n^3+n) log(n+2)). Apply the general-density SAT assumption.

4. Binary search the monotone threshold b in [0,n] with O(log(n+1)) queries. Then keep the optimum threshold and fix original deletion bits sequentially, trying zero whenever an optimum extension remains. This uses at most n more queries and O(n) additional unit clauses, and produces an optimum vertex set.

5. The total is A(n)L^{O(1)} time and polynomial space, with the separately reported formalization bound available under its own assumption. The paired counting entry additionally counts optimum solutions.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The scale is n, not the optimum solution size. This deduction neither supplies nor assumes a linear-vertex kernel for the solution-budget parameter.
- The result is for feedback vertex sets in tournaments, not feedback arc sets or arbitrary directed graphs.
- No binary-weight extension or latest-best comparison is asserted. Preserve the fixed width of three and the original vertex measure.

The derivation must preserve the objective and account for the encoding length of numerical values; a decision consequence alone does not establish the stated optimization bound.
